title: Attendance policies
subtitle: Employee groups, attendance points and discipline, the overtime summary and the country rule packs behind your policies.

groups.hint: An employee belongs to at most one group on a date. A policy scoped to a group applies to its members on the days they are in it.
groups.dialogHint: Groups are organisation-wide: Office staff, Sales staff, Field staff…
groups.emptyHint: Create groups to give office, sales or field staff their own attendance policy.
groups.deleteHint: Its memberships are removed with it. Attendance is not recalculated: no policy uses the group.
groups.deleteBlocked: Policies scoped to this group: {{count}}. Delete or end them first, or set the group inactive.

members.title: Members of {{name}}
members.hint: Memberships are dated: the policy of the group applies from the first day to the last day included.
members.moveHint: An employee already in a group without an end date leaves it the day before; any other overlap is refused.
members.endedOthers: Earlier memberships ended to make room: {{count}}
members.recalcHint: The attendance of these employees is being recalculated.
members.emptyHint: Nobody is in this group today.
members.endHint: The employee stays in the group up to and including this day.
members.removeHint: The membership is deleted as if it never existed; the days it covered are recalculated.

points.hint: Points are counted under each employee's policy on the as-of date, over the policy's rolling window. Excused days earn nothing.
points.offHint: Points are off for this policy.
points.emptyHint: Nobody matches the filters on this date.

overtime.hint: Overtime of the month under each employee's policy on its last day. Weekly overtime counts the ISO weeks ending on a Sunday of the month, net of the daily overtime; weighted = minutes × the policy's rates.
overtime.emptyHint: Nobody matches the filters in this month.

packs.hint: Statutory working-time figures per country. A pack pre-fills a new policy and drives the compliance warnings; it never changes a policy by itself. Sector and contract rules vary — confirm with counsel.
